claim.why_it_matters: Same lost choice indicator as Format 1. Without the bars the bracket reads as 'at most one of ON EXCEPTION / NOT ON EXCEPTION', but 14.9.10.4 GR 20 c)/d) and GR 21 b) describe behaviour in which both phrases may be present on the same DELETE FILE statement. Legal source is made to look illegal.

verdict.reasoning:
CONFIRMED on independent inspection of the rendered glyphs at 300 dpi (E:/Temp/specrecon/v635/spec_p635.png, cropped and magnified 3x over the Format 2 block). WHAT I SEE PRINTED: on the left of the two stacked EXCEPTION alternatives there are TWO distinct vertical strokes side by side - the outer one is a square bracket with horizontal serifs turning right at top and bottom (a full-height '['), and immediately inside it, separated by a clear white gap, a plain full-height vertical bar with NO serifs at either end. The right side mirrors this exactly: a plain unserifed full-height bar, then a square bracket ']' with serifs turning left at top and bottom. Both the bracket and the bar span the full height of BOTH alternatives. That is precisely the printed form '[| ... |]'. The identical construction appears in Format 1 (record) on the same page around INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY, which I cropped and inspected separately. So the claim's description of the PDF is accurate, not an artifact of low resolution or of an OCR guess.

THE MARKDOWN: verified verbatim in the canonical transcription specs/ISO_COBOL.md at lines 26333-26338 (not merely in the extracted page-635.md slice, to rule out the slicer dropping content). The block is exactly as quoted. There are no '|' bars inside the brackets, and there is NO '> **Figure notes ...**' annotation attached to either DELETE format that might have recorded the choice indicator in prose instead. The claim misquotes neither source.

MEANING CHANGES - this is the decisive point, and it is normative, not typographic. ISO/IEC 1989:2023 5.2.6.2 (Brackets): brackets indicate that the enclosed syntax element 'or ONE of the alternatives contained within the brackets may be explicitly specified' - i.e. at most one. ISO 5.2.6.4 (Choice indicators): 'Choice indicators are a pair of bars, |, that enclose a portion of a general format. ... When enclosed by brackets, ZERO OR MORE of the alternatives contained within the choice indicators shall be specified, but any single alternative may be specified only once. ... The alternatives may be specified in any order.' The bars are therefore load-bearing: with them the format permits BOTH ON EXCEPTION and NOT ON EXCEPTION on one DELETE FILE statement; without them it permits at most one. The degraded transcription rejects legal source.

CORROBORATED BY THE PROSE ON THE SAME STATEMENT: 14.9.10.4 GR 21 b) reads 'If the NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase is specified in the DELETE FILE statement, control is transferred to the imperative-statement-4 specified in the NOT ON EXCEPTION phrase. THE ON EXCEPTION PHRASE IS IGNORED, IF IT IS SPECIFIED.' That sentence is unreachable and meaningless unless both phrases can coexist on the same statement, which settles the reading independently of the glyphs.

SELF-INCONSISTENCY WITHIN THE TRANSCRIPTION: specs/ISO_COBOL.md already has a correct, established convention for exactly this construct. ADD Format 1 at lines 25477-25478 renders the same bracket-plus-choice-indicator as '⎡|  ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-1      |⎤' / '⎣|  NOT ON SIZE ERROR imperative-statement-2  |⎦', followed by an explicit '> **Figure notes (ISO 5.2.6.4)**' paragraph spelling out that both phrases may appear. Page 635 uses the bare-bracket form with no bars and no note. So this is an isolated transcription defect against the file's own convention, not a limitation of the notation - which also makes the fix mechanical.

RULED OUT: not reflow (nothing adjacent contains the bars); not a page break, wrapping, or hyphenation (the figure is wholly on page 635); not cosmetic formatting (5.2.6.2 vs 5.2.6.4 assign different normative meanings); not a misquote of either source.
verdict.corrected_description: Claim confirmed as stated; two refinements for precision. (1) The PDF glyphs are exactly as described - a full-height square bracket with serifs at top and bottom, plus a separate unserifed full-height vertical bar immediately inside it, on BOTH sides, spanning both stacked alternatives: '[| ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-3 / NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-4 |]'. The transcription drops both bars, and additionally degrades the bracket itself (it draws only the top corners '⌐'/'¬' with bare verticals below, never closing the bottom); the bracket degradation is cosmetic, the lost bars are the normative defect. (2) The strongest supporting citation is 14.9.10.4 GR 21 b), whose clause 'The ON EXCEPTION phrase is ignored, if it is specified' is unreachable unless both phrases may coexist; GR 20 c)/d) are merely consistent with that reading rather than decisive, since each speaks only to whether ON EXCEPTION is or is not specified. Governing notation rules are ISO 5.2.6.2 (brackets = at most one) and 5.2.6.4 (bars within brackets = zero or more, any order, each at most once). FIX: render the block using the convention the file already uses at ADD Format 1 (lines 25477-25478) - '⎡| ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-3 |⎤' / '⎣| NOT ON EXCEPTION imperative-statement-4 |⎦' - and attach a 'Figure notes (ISO 5.2.6.4)' annotation. The sibling defect in DELETE Format 1 (INVALID KEY / NOT INVALID KEY) on the same page is identical and must be fixed in the same change set.
